q: The Linearisation theorem of Sternberg (smooth conjugacy near a hyperbolic fixed point) strengthens Hartman-Grobman by providing a smooth (C^∞) conjugacy when:
opts: The eigenvalues satisfy non-resonance conditions: no eigenvalue λⱼ equals a monomial λ₁^{m₁}…λₙ^{mₙ} with Σmᵢ ≥ 2
The fixed point is asymptotically stable
exp: Sternberg's theorem: if the eigenvalues of Df(0) satisfy non-resonance conditions (no resonances among them), then f is C^∞ (even C^ω)-conjugate to its linear part. Resonances obstruct smooth linearisation and lead to normal forms (Dulac, Poincaré normal form theory).
